text: Given a live/sandbox tenant with at least two clients that each have at least one site, When halopsa_sites_list({client_id: <clientA>}) is called against the real API, Then only client A's sites are returned, not client B's
steps: Obtain or set up a HaloPSA sandbox/dev tenant with at least two clients, each with at least one site
Call halopsa_sites_list with client_id set to client A's id
expect: Every returned site belongs to client A; no site belonging to client B appears in the response
notes: Needs a real/sandbox HaloPSA tenant with multi-client site data; none available in this dev session either (no HALOPSA_CLIENT_ID/SECRET configured, no network access to a tenant). Still untested/local blind spot, not a pass. Partial independent evidence: the unit test 'should forward an optional client_id filter to the API' (sites.test.ts, used as evidence for TC-HALO-012) proves client_id is correctly passed through to client.sites.list({client_id, pageSize}) — i.e. the wiring is correct — but does not prove HaloPSA's own API actually narrows results by it, which is what this case asks. Left for manual verification once a tenant is available.

text: Security (OWASP API1:2023 BOLA): Given two separate mocked credential contexts (tenant A, tenant B) bound via runWithCredentials, When tenant A calls any of the five new tools, Then the resolved SDK client instance and its mock data are strictly tenant A's, and tenant B's mocked contacts/sites are never reachable from tenant A's call
tests: src/__tests__/domains/users.test.ts::multi-tenant isolation::should never resolve another tenant's client or data (PRD-20396, OWASP API1 BOLA)
evidence: vitest: users.test.ts > multi-tenant isolation > should never resolve another tenant's client or data (PRD-20396, OWASP API1 BOLA) — PASS. Two concurrent calls (Promise.all) to the real (unmocked) usersHandler.handleCall, bound to different AsyncLocalStorage contexts (tenant-a / tenant-b), each tenant's result contained only its own contact's emailaddress and never the other tenant's. NOTE on scope: this test substitutes a direct AsyncLocalStorage harness for the literal runWithCredentials()+credentialKey()-cache path described in the design text, to keep the test deterministic without invoking the real HaloPSA SDK/network. The generic cache mechanism itself is unmodified by this ticket and is already covered by this repo's own src/__tests__/client.test.ts (credential caching, placeholder handling). What this test specifically proves — and what's actually new in this ticket — is that the five new tools' handler code has no shared/retained state across concurrent calls in different credential contexts. | npm test (vitest run) — full run: 247 passed, 0 failed, 0 regressions vs. baseline (216 passed); npm run typecheck exit 0; npm run lint exit 0; npm run build exit 0 (.tdd/final.json, .tdd/gate-selftest.json)
